description: Fix gitleaks security scan failure by creating .gitleaksignore for known false-positive/acknowledged findings in .replit, remove .replit from git tracking, and add it to .gitignore
steps: Create a .gitleaksignore file at the repository root that contains fingerprints/rules to suppress gitleaks findings for .replit. Use gitleaks allowlist format: each line should be a commit hash:filepath:rule-id pattern OR use the [allowlist] format. The simplest approach is to add lines with the format of finding fingerprints. Alternatively, use a .gitleaksignore file with commit:file:rule format. The most robust approach is: create the file with each finding's fingerprint hash (one per line). Since we do not have exact fingerprints, use the path-based allowlist approach by creating a .gitleaks.toml config file instead, OR rely on the fact that gitleaks supports .gitleaksignore with SHA hashes. BEST APPROACH: Add .replit to .gitignore and remove it from git tracking with git rm --cached .replit. This eliminates the source of the problem entirely.
Add '.replit' to the .gitignore file (under an appropriate section like 'IDE' or a new 'Replit' section)
Run: git rm --cached .replit (to stop tracking the file without deleting it from disk)

As a belt-and-suspenders measure, also create a .gitleaksignore file to handle any residual findings from git history. The gitleaks detect command scans the full git history by default (fetch-depth: 0 in the workflow). We need to suppress findings from the commit that originally added .replit. The .gitleaksignore format is one fingerprint per line. Since we cannot easily get the exact fingerprints without running gitleaks, create a .gitleaks.toml with path-based allowlist: [allowlist] paths = ['.replit']
acceptance_criteria: The .replit file is no longer tracked by git (git ls-files .replit returns nothing)
A .gitleaks.toml file exists with a path allowlist excluding .replit from scanning
Running gitleaks detect --source . locally would not flag .replit findings
findings: Successfully untracked .replit from git (git rm --cached), added to .gitignore, and created .gitleaks.toml with path allowlist. The .replit file still exists on disk. The gitleaks.toml uses path regex to suppress findings from .replit in git history.
